transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Can we just pause for a second? I think we’re talking past each other a little. Maybe if we spell out exactly what each team is proposing, it’ll help us see where there’s overlap.

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: Alright, let's lay it all out. Each team, just spell out your proposal in plain English—no jargon, no hedging. And if you're worried about your role, say so. We can't fix what we don't surface.

transcript.text: We’re not here to air feelings. Spell out your proposal, Lucía. No hedging, no history. Then James’ team does the same. I’ll decide who leads. Everyone else, save commentary unless you’re directly asked. Understood?

transcript.text: Alright, here’s what our team is proposing: we focus on streamlining the handoff process between dispatch and warehouse so orders get packed and out faster. I’d coordinate with both teams to track bottlenecks and report daily. If anyone sees a gap or isn’t sure about their role in this, say it now. Better to be clear than stuck later.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Can we just make sure we’re looking at this from the user’s side? I think both proposals need to spell out where the pain points actually are, otherwise we risk talking in circles.

transcript.text: Alright, here’s the basics from my team. We’ll handle upgrading the signal controls, double-check the wiring plans, and report any snags by end of day. If anyone’s unclear on who’s doing what, speak up now—better to sort it.

transcript.text: I think É​lise has a point. Maybe before we decide, can we be more specific about where the main problems actually show up for users? Otherwise, we might just be patching symptoms.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Do we have any recent user feedback or data showing where the biggest delays or issues are actually happening? It might help us focus the proposal a bit more.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: Have we actually looked at the recent complaints or feedback from users? If we’re deciding between these, it might help to see which proposal addresses the main issues better. I’m not sure I’ve seen that part yet.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: If it helps, I can pull up the last batch of user complaints from support logs. Might make it easier to see which issues each proposal actually addresses. Should I do that?

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: If Amitesh can get those logs now, that’d help. No point debating in circles until we see where the users are having the biggest issues.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: Alright, give me a minute—I'll pull up the latest support logs now. Should I just read out the top three complaints, or do folks want the whole list?

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Let’s hear the top three, Amitesh. That should give us a clearer picture. Then we can see which proposal actually hits those pain points.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: I agree, getting those top complaints out loud could help us focus. Once Amitesh reads them, maybe we can talk through how each proposal covers those points. That way it’s less about which team and more about what actually fixes things.

transcript.name: Park Jae-Won
transcript.text: I’m not interested in more back-and-forth. Both teams have had time to review the data. Choose the lead for each proposal now. If you can’t, I’ll choose for you. We move forward in two minutes. That’s it.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Honestly, I think Lucía should lead the proposal that focuses on the user pain points. She knows the feedback best and can keep us grounded in what matters for the people actually using the service. Unless someone else feels strongly, I’d back her on that.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: I think Lucía should lead too. She’s been closest to the user feedback and can help us stay on track with what matters. Makes sense to me.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: I’m fine with Lucía taking the lead, as long as roles are spelled out. Just want to avoid confusion on who’s responsible for what. That’s all from me.

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: Lucía, sounds like you’ve got the group’s trust for this. Anyone here have a real objection, or can we call that settled? If you’ve got reservations, better to say it now than grumble later.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: No objections here. Lucía’s close to the feedback and seems like the right person to lead. I’d just ask that we spell out roles clearly for everyone so there’s no mixed messages.

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: Alright, Lucía’s leading, that’s clear. But before we close it—can we get a quick rundown on who’s covering which piece? Just so no one’s caught off guard halfway through. If you’re unsure about your bit, say so now.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Just to be clear, I’ll take care of mapping the main user journey and flagging any points where feedback highlights confusion or delays. If anyone else needs me to cover something specific, let me know now.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: I’ll keep tabs on the control system upgrades and wiring. If anyone needs a hand with the technical details, just flag it. Let’s not let things slip through the cracks.

transcript.name: Park Jae-Won
transcript.text: Everyone’s roles are set. No more excuses, no more second-guessing. Lucía, deliver results. If anyone’s unclear about their piece, speak now. Otherwise, I expect updates on schedule. Understood?

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Just so it's clear—I'll review all compliance and documentation steps, and if anything seems off, I’ll flag it right away. If anyone needs a double-check on process stuff, just let me know.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Just to confirm, I’ll handle the data pipeline checks and flag anything odd in the transfer logs. If anyone sees a data issue, let me know right away.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: Just to confirm, I’ll keep handling the data review and flag anything odd in the reports. If there’s something else you need me to watch for, let me know now.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Just want to double-check—does anyone feel unsure about their part, or see any gaps we missed? Better to say it now than hit a snag later.
